extracted.intended_audience: UK government officials running public consultations; consultees, organisations and stakeholders preparing consultation responses
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for producing effective responses to UK government public consultations and for designing consultations that meet Cabinet Office standards. Emphasises plain language, proportionality, targeted engagement, evidence, and timeliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear and concise
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mirrors the government's plain-language standard: use plain English, define technical terms, limit length to what is necessary, and structure the response so a non-expert reader can navigate it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purposeful
rubrics_metrics.description: Consult only when necessary; not on settled matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government should only consult where it will inform decision-making; consultees should avoid raising matters outside the consultation's purpose or on issues already decided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informative
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consultations should include sufficient background and impact assessment information; responses should engage with that context and provide evidence on impacts where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part of engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Use informal, iterative approaches and digital tools as part of wider engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consultation is one element of broader engagement. Responses (and consultation design) should consider iterative dialogue and digital engagement channels where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportionate duration
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set consultation lengths that reflect the significance and complexity of the issue; consultees should expect and respect proportional timeframes while allowing extra time for groups who need it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeted
rubrics_metrics.description: Reach affected populations and representative groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design consultation and target outreach to those affected and representative organisations; responses should show awareness of which populations are impacted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerate of groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Adapt methods (e.g., charities need more time).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust consultation methods and timelines to accommodate different groups' needs—allow longer periods or alternative formats where participants (e.g., charities, small organisations) require them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-agreed
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before publishing a consultation or its materials, seek necessary collective sign-offs or approvals to ensure readiness and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitates scrutiny
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish responses alongside the original consultation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make responses publicly available alongside consultation materials to enable public scrutiny; this implies that responses should be drafted with potential public visibility in mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish responses within 12 weeks of consultation closing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to a 12-week target for publishing responses to ensure timely feedback to consultees and transparency about decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid election periods
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid initiating consultations during election periods to prevent politicisation and ensure fair consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain English and defined technical terms (response-focused)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use plain English with technical terms defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep language simple, define specialist terms, and write so non-experts can understand the response; limit verbosity to what is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer the specific consultation questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective responses answer the questions asked, not adjacent issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage directly with the consultation's questions (referencing question numbers where possible), rather than introducing unrelated topics; focused answers are more usable to decision-makers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide evidence proportionate to the issue
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide evidence proportionate to the issue; detailed evidence for substantial issues, brief for narrower questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match the amount and depth of supporting evidence to the scale and importance of the point being made; cite sources or data where relevant and feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target responses to the government's stated decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify which decision points the response addresses and how the proposed change would affect outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make explicit which policy decision or option you are commenting on and explain the likely effects, costs, benefits or unintended consequences of the proposed change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure responses for non-expert readers
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure the response so a non-expert reader can navigate it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clear headings, summaries, and logical organisation so that readers unfamiliar with the topic can find key points quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge the consultation's stated purpose and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the response acknowledge the consultation's stated purpose and scope?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly recognise and work within the consultation's remit; where you propose out-of-scope changes, explain why they are relevant or suggest alternative routes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assume public publication (public-facing drafting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Draft responses with the expectation they will be published and publicly scrutinised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid including unnecessary confidential or sensitive material; where confidentiality is required, follow the consultation's guidance on how to make such requests.
